svg.title: Figure 5. Built-up beams: loose, partially connected and bonded
svg.desc: Three panels for a beam made of two equal layers with a central load. (a) Strain through the depth at midspan: loose layers bend separately, each with its own neutral axis, so the strain jumps at the interface; a bonded beam has one straight strain line through the whole depth; a partially connected beam lies in between, with a smaller jump. (b) Slip between the layers along the span, divided by the loose end slip: largest at the supports and zero at midspan, and much smaller and confined near the supports as the connection parameter alpha L grows. (c) Effective bending stiffness divided by the loose value against alpha L on a log scale: it rises from 1 for a loose stack to 4 for a fully bonded one, with most of the gain between alpha L of about 1 and 30.
